items.title: JJ Johnson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Jamey Aebersold came to me a few years ago and said, 'J.J. I would like to publish a book of your solos... We came up with ten, and he published them'

ctx.x: David will ask you about some other recordings in just a minute, but I have another favorite that I want to ask you. Out of your numerous, numerous compositions over the years, do you have particular favorites among those?

Not really. Not really. Taking two steps backward, getting back on this other thing we were talking about, Jamey Aebersold came to me a few years ago and said, "J.J. I would like to publish a book of your solos on your recording projects. What I would like for you to do is get all of your recordings out, listen to them very carefully, and pick out ten of the solos you consider to be your best efforts ever." It was the most difficult project I have ever undertaken. Listening to your own solos over and over and…

Does a particular performance event – at a festival or in a club – does a particular performance event or several performance events stand out for you as you look back over your career over the years? [Do] any of them seem more special?

items.title: Jamey Aebersold interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 26, 2022
items.q: I had a cassette of J.J. Johnson with Horace Silver and Woody Show and Joe Henderson in my — and I had a cassette player back then and I had that cassette.

ctx.x: I must say that when you said Charlie Parker and I don’t know what to think about that, if you see over my shoulder you see your “All Bird” book. When I bought that and tried to play along with it, I said, “I don’t know what to think about this except I’m not ready for it.”

Let me show you something. You know musicians, we’ve always aspired to be able to play fast, fast, fast and being able to play what we’re actually thinking at a fast tempo and make it swing, make it cook. Here’s the fall of 1994, J.J. Johnson. I’ll read it to you: I’ll read it to you. He says, “Dear Jamey, Leaving for Japan in a few days. Chops are just awful.
